requirements.statement: 'Amend this notification' on a submitted notification's view page, and the Amend action on its card in the set's notification list, open an amend confirmation page at the notification's own amend route, in every set that amends (live animals, germinal products and plants): its title and level-1 heading are 'Amend notification', it asks 'Are you sure you want to change this notification?', and nothing changes until the trader confirms.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 asks the trader to confirm before reopening a submitted notification; the 9 October afternoon ruling keeps that confirmation as a page carrying the pop-up's wording, and puts every amendment, plants' included, behind it (c-190, c-manage-notifications-001).
requirements.deltaNote: Today there is no amend confirmation: the card's Amend is a form button that starts the amendment straight away (trace-animals-fit-p3-027, trace-animals-fit-p3-028), as plants' card Amend does (repo-plantsfrontend-p3-134), and the view page offers no Amend (trace-e2e-p14-050).

requirements.statement: On the amend confirmation page, 'Yes, continue' is a button that submits the page's form (with the CSRF crumb) and starts the amendment, and 'No, go back' is a link-styled control that returns to the notification's view page without changing anything; the page's Back link goes to the view page too.
requirements.why: The trader confirms or backs out of amending without losing their place; a state change is a form post (c-189).

requirements.statement: With JavaScript, 'Amend this notification' and 'Cancel amend' open their confirmations as modal dialogs over the current page instead of going to the confirmation pages: hidden until opened, role dialog with aria-modal, labelled by the heading (the amend dialog also described by its question), each with a Close (X) button labelled 'Close' for screen readers and an overlay; Close, the overlay and the dialog's 'No, go back' or 'Go back' dismiss it without acting and leave the trader where they were. Built for live animals, germinal products and plants only if design makes a strong case; otherwise dropped.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 confirms in place. The 9 October afternoon ruling holds the pop-ups back: GOV.UK Frontend has no modal, MoJ's modal dialog is not accepted and has no fallback without JavaScript, and no custom JavaScript is written to copy the prototype (c-190).
requirements.blockedBy: Design answers design question 9 (the amend and cancel-amendment pop-ups) in the waiting-on-design theme; the expected answer is that they are not built, and the increment is then dropped.

requirements.statement: Confirming an amendment ('Yes, continue' on the amend confirmation page, reached from the view page or the card's Amend) takes the trader to the notification's review page (the amend review), not to its overview hub, in every set that amends: live animals, germinal products and plants (plants' own review page).
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 opens an amendment on the review page so the trader sees every answer and its Change link at once; the 9 October afternoon ruling keeps this outcome and gives plants the same landing.
requirements.deltaNote: Today Amend posts to /notifications/{id}/amend and redirects to the overview hub showing 'Amending' (trace-animals-fit-p3-027, trace-e2e-p14-053, repo-tests-p4-098); the review page is one step further, behind Review and submit (trace-animals-fit-p3-031, repo-tests-p3-086). Plants takes the same landing on its own review page (ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p3-043).

requirements.statement: Amending moves a SUBMITTED notification to AMEND, keeps its reference and original submitted time, stores a full independent snapshot of the submitted content and fulfilments, and records a NotificationAmendmentRequested event carrying the status history and the actor; an unknown reference gets 404 and any status but SUBMITTED gets 400.
requirements.why: The submitted version must survive the amendment so cancelling can restore it and other services see the change.
requirements.deltaNote: The backend amend endpoint already does this (repo-backend-p2-090, repo-backend-p2-094, repo-backend-p2-098), proven end to end (trace-e2e-p14-070).

requirements.statement: Answers changed during an amendment are saved to the notification record (status stays AMEND) as the trader goes, and are not visible as the submitted version until resubmitted.
requirements.why: The real service persists every save; the prototype's session-only amendment cannot express persistence.
requirements.deltaNote: Saving keeps a notification in AMEND (repo-backend-p2-111), and a changed value survives leaving the cancel page (trace-animals-fit-p3-042).

requirements.statement: A notification being amended shows the status tag 'Amend' in the shared status strip, changed once for every set (live animals, germinal products and plants).
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 names the state 'Amend'; the 9 October afternoon ruling changes the shared strip's label in every set at once.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the tag reads 'Amending' (yellow) on the hub, review and cancel pages (trace-animals-fit-p3-029, trace-e2e-p14-031).

requirements.statement: During an amendment, the review page and every question page show an Amend status bar above the caption and heading: the 'Amend' tag, the reference, and a link-styled 'Cancel amend' control that goes to the cancel-amendment confirmation page. It is a change to the shared status strip, so live animals, germinal products and plants all get it at once. Whether the hub's own status line carries it is req-782's.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 lets the trader abandon the amendment from wherever they are in it; the 9 October afternoon ruling makes this the one change to the shared strip, and sends 'Cancel amend' to the confirmation page.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a 'Cancel amendment' link sits under the review page heading only; the hub and question pages offer no way to cancel (trace-animals-fit-p3-032, trace-animals-fit-p3-029-m1, trace-e2e-p14-055).

requirements.statement: The amend review has no page-header actions (no Amend this notification, no Copy as new), no Import reference numbers section and no Date submitted line.
requirements.why: During an amendment the status bar replaces the view page's header.
requirements.deltaNote: Today's amending view shows no Copy as new or Delete under its heading (trace-e2e-p14-032-m1) and has no Import reference numbers section or Date submitted line.

requirements.statement: The amend review is editable, with a Change link on every card (the first going to the origin of the import), and its Back link goes to the notification's overview hub.
requirements.why: Amending means changing the submitted answers.
requirements.deltaNote: The amending review already has Change links on every card and a Back link to the hub (trace-e2e-p14-032, trace-animals-fit-p3-034).

requirements.statement: While a submitted notification is being amended, each page the overview links to, including a question page opened from the amend review, ends with a primary 'Save and return' button that saves and goes to the amend review (which shows the changed answer), a secondary 'Save and continue' button that saves and goes to the next page, and a link-styled 'Save and return to overview' button, with no cancel link. The buttons post the real service's own fields (exit=hub and ?change=1 stay); no action=review|continue|hub field is added. The party pickers, the CPH number page and the permanent address page, which DR1 rule (b) keeps to the primary button outside amend, show 'Save and return' and 'Save and continue' only, without 'Save and return to overview'. Plants' save actions get the same three amend controls, and its pickers the same two buttons, in the same increment.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 lets the trader return to the review straight after a change, or carry on.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a Change link opens the question with ?change=1 and saving returns to the notification view with no choice of where to go (trace-e2e-p14-047, repo-tests-p3-079).

requirements.statement: During an amendment, question pages keep the journey's usual Back links (the origin of the import back to the notification type page, arrival details back to the overview hub), not a link to the amend review.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 does not change Back links for an amendment.

requirements.statement: During an amendment, question pages are prefilled with the notification's saved answers and keep their usual copy (for example Arrival details: arrival date at port of entry with a d/m/yyyy date picker, port of entry search, means of transport, transport identification and document reference).
requirements.why: The trader changes only what needs changing.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a Change link during an amendment opens the question with the saved answers (repo-tests-p3-079, trace-e2e-p14-046).

requirements.statement: Continue on the amend review is held while any answer is invalid or incomplete (such as an arrival date outside 7 days back to 6 months ahead): the trader stays on the amend review and, as Design Release 2.1 draws it, no error summary or error message is shown. The draft review's error summary is not carried over to the amend review. Plants' amend review holds Continue the same way, in the same increment.
requirements.why: A resubmitted amendment must be complete and valid, and the hold itself meets that constraint; Design Release 2.1 draws the refused Continue as a silent hold and DR1 judged nothing about the amend review, so the prototype wins (c-201).
requirements.deltaNote: Today an amendment reaches the declaration only once every task row is fulfilled (repo-tests-p3-085).

requirements.statement: Continue on a valid amend review goes to the Declaration page; ticking the declaration and pressing Continue resubmits the amendment.
requirements.why: An amendment is resubmitted through the same declaration as a first submission.
requirements.deltaNote: Continue on the amending review already leads to the Declaration, and ticking it resubmits (repo-tests-p3-088, repo-tests-p3-091, trace-e2e-p14-056).

requirements.statement: Resubmitting an amendment shows the ordinary 'Import notification submitted' confirmation with the notification's existing reference and no wording about an amendment; the same record becomes Submitted again, read only, with the edited answers, the dashboard shows the amended answers, and it can be amended again.
requirements.why: An amendment replaces the submitted notification rather than creating a second one.
requirements.deltaNote: Resubmission already lands on the submitted confirmation and the notification is Submitted, read only and amendable again with the edited value (repo-tests-p3-092, trace-e2e-p14-057, trace-e2e-p14-059).

requirements.statement: The cancel-amendment confirmation page's title and level-1 heading are 'Are you sure you want to cancel this amendment?', with no caption, in every set that amends (live animals, germinal products and plants).
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's wording for cancelling an amendment, carried onto the page by the 9 October afternoon ruling; on a page the heading is the level-1 heading, where the pop-up drew a level-2.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the cancel-amend page's title and level-1 heading are 'Cancel this amendment?' (repo-frontend-p3-080, trace-e2e-p14-035), in plants too (repo-plantsfrontend-p3-100).

requirements.statement: The cancel-amendment confirmation page shows no paragraph explaining that changes will be discarded and the submitted version restored, in every set that amends.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's cancel-amendment confirmation has no description line, and the 9 October afternoon ruling carries that onto the page.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the page says 'Your changes since you started amending will be discarded and the submitted version restored.' (repo-frontend-p3-081, trace-e2e-p14-036), as plants' does (repo-plantsfrontend-p3-101).

requirements.statement: The cancel-amendment confirm button reads 'Yes, cancel amendment' and is a standard (not warning) primary button.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree on this button.
requirements.deltaNote: Today's cancel-amend page already has a standard 'Yes, cancel amendment' button (repo-frontend-p3-082, trace-animals-fit-p3-038).

requirements.statement: The cancel-amendment confirmation page's way back is a link-styled 'Go back' that returns to the notification's view (the amend review while amending; plants' check answers view) and leaves the amendment in progress, replacing the secondary button 'No, return to notification', in every set that amends.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's wording and pattern for not cancelling; as a page at today's route, it goes back where today's way back goes.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the way back is a secondary button-styled link 'No, return to notification' to the notification view (repo-frontend-p3-083, trace-e2e-p14-039), and the same in plants (repo-plantsfrontend-p3-104).

requirements.statement: 'Cancel amend' (in the Amend status bar and beside Continue on the amend review) and the card's 'Cancel amendment' go to the cancel-amendment confirmation page at today's route (/notifications/{id}/cancel-amend in each set), which carries only the confirmation's heading and buttons: no journey strip and no Back link.
requirements.why: The 9 October afternoon ruling keeps the cancel confirmation as a separate page at today's route carrying the pop-up's wording, so the page holds what the pop-up held.
requirements.deltaNote: Today 'Cancel amendment' is a link under the review heading and on the card, reaching a page at /notifications/{id}/cancel-amend with the Amending journey strip and a Back link to the notification view (repo-frontend-p3-078, repo-frontend-p3-138, trace-e2e-p14-034, trace-e2e-p14-037); plants has the same page with a Back link (repo-plantsfrontend-p3-099, repo-plantsfrontend-p3-105).

requirements.statement: Confirming the cancellation discards every edit made during the amendment, restores the submitted content and fulfilments, returns the notification to SUBMITTED with its original submitted time, records one NotificationAmendmentCancelled event, and takes the trader to that notification's view page, read only and showing Submitted.
requirements.why: Cancelling must leave the notification exactly as it was submitted.
requirements.deltaNote: Cancel-amend already restores the snapshot and returns to the read-only Submitted view (repo-backend-p2-105, trace-e2e-p14-045, trace-animals-fit-p3-047).

requirements.statement: After an amendment is cancelled, the view page shows no success banner; the redirect to it keeps ?cancelled=1 in its address, as today, in every set that amends.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 returns to the view page without a message; the 9 October ruling keeps ?cancelled=1, because the prototype never decides URL shapes.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the view opens at ?cancelled=1 with a 'Success' banner reading 'The amendment has been cancelled and the submitted version restored.' (trace-animals-fit-p3-044, trace-animals-fit-p3-045, repo-tests-p3-080): the address stays, the banner goes. Plants already redirects with cancelled=1 and its cancel feature sets no banner (repo-plantsfrontend-p3-110, repo-plantsfrontend-p3-113).

requirements.statement: Opening or posting cancel amendment for a notification that is not being amended changes nothing and returns the trader to the set's own notification list with no message, in every set that amends.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 guards the route silently; the 9 October afternoon ruling sends every 'overall dashboard' destination, this one included, to the set's own list.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a Submitted notification is redirected to its view page (plants: its check answers view), and any other status to the set's list (repo-frontend-p3-079, repo-frontend-p3-087, repo-plantsfrontend-p3-109).

requirements.statement: When copy as new, cancel amendment or delete fails to save, the page the trader came from is shown again with HTTP 500 and the recoverable-error banner, in every set that has the action.
requirements.why: A real save can fail; the prototype cannot express that.
requirements.deltaNote: Each controller already re-renders with 500 and the recoverable-error banner (repo-frontend-p3-076, repo-frontend-p3-088, repo-frontend-p3-102).

requirements.statement: In the animals sets (live animals and germinal products), Copy as new goes straight, with no confirmation, to the new draft's overview hub titled 'Overview', which has no Back link and no banner announcing the copy.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree that copying is immediate and quiet.
requirements.deltaNote: Copy already redirects straight to the new notification's overview with no banner (trace-e2e-p3-073, trace-e2e-p3-077, trace-animals-fit-p2-075).

requirements.statement: A copy is a new notification saved at once as a Draft, with its own new reference (same GBN-AG prefix, fresh suffix); the source is unchanged, the copy is independent of it, every copy is distinct, and a NotificationCreated event (carrying the acting user's organisation id to resolve address-book parties) is recorded for the copy only.
requirements.why: Copying must never alter or merge with the notification it came from.
requirements.deltaNote: The backend copy endpoint already makes a new DRAFT with a new reference and leaves the source alone (repo-backend-p2-042, repo-backend-p2-044, trace-e2e-p14-074).

requirements.statement: A copy carries over the origin of the import: country of origin, whether a region of origin code is required, and the region of origin code with its suffix.
requirements.why: These describe the trade, not the shipment, so they usually repeat.
requirements.deltaNote: The copy mapper keeps them (repo-backend-p2-047) and the copy's origin page comes back prefilled (trace-animals-fit-p2-078).

requirements.statement: A copy carries over the internal reference number, in the notification record as well as on the page.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 carries it over with the import details.
requirements.deltaNote: The backend copy mapper clears the internal reference in the notification record (repo-backend-p2-048), though the copy's origin page shows it from the copied fulfilments (trace-animals-fit-p2-078).

requirements.statement: A copy carries over what is being imported: the commodity (id, code and name), the commodity selections, the selected species and the notification type (worked out from the copied answers when missing).
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 marks What are you importing? Complete on the copy.
requirements.deltaNote: The backend copy mapper keeps the commodity name and each complement's type but clears every complement's species list (repo-backend-p2-049, repo-backend-p2-050, repo-backend-p2-051).

requirements.statement: A copy does not carry over the number of animals, the number of packages or the net weight: the copy's commodity details show To do, its Animals total reads 0 and its Packages/boxes total shows no figure.
requirements.why: Counts are specific to each shipment.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the copy's overview carries the totals (1 animal, 5 packages) and marks Commodity details Complete (trace-e2e-p3-075, trace-e2e-p13-109, trace-animals-fit-p2-077), though the copy mapper clears them in the record (repo-backend-p2-051).

requirements.statement: A copy does not carry over animal identifiers (ear tags, passports and the like): the copy's Identification details show To do.
requirements.why: Identifiers belong to the animals in one shipment.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the copy's Identification details show Complete (trace-e2e-p13-109, trace-e2e-p3-075), though the copy mapper drops identifiers from the record (repo-backend-p2-052).

requirements.statement: A copy carries over the main reason for import and its follow-ups: internal market purpose, transhipment destination country, transit exit border control post, transit destination country, and the temporary admission exit date and port of exit.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 marks Main import reason Complete on the copy.
requirements.deltaNote: The backend copy mapper keeps the reason, purpose, destination country and port of exit but clears the exit date (repo-backend-p2-053, repo-backend-p2-059, repo-backend-p2-062).

requirements.statement: A copy carries over the additional animal details: what the animals are certified for, whether unweaned animals are included, and the storage temperature.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 marks Additional details Complete on the copy.
requirements.deltaNote: The backend copy mapper keeps certified-for but clears the unweaned animals answer (repo-backend-p2-054).

requirements.statement: When copying a live-animals notification, a certified-for value that is no longer an option is mapped to a current one: 'Breeding' and 'Breeding and/or production' become 'Further keeping', 'Slaughter' stays 'Slaughter', and any other value not offered becomes 'Further keeping'.
requirements.why: A copy must not carry an answer the trader can no longer choose.

requirements.statement: A copy carries over the roles and addresses (place of origin, consignor, consignee, importer and place of destination, each in full as stored), the CPH number and the permanent address details.
requirements.why: Trading partners usually repeat between shipments.
requirements.deltaNote: The copy mapper keeps every party, the CPH number and the whole fulfilments payload (repo-backend-p2-055, repo-backend-p2-058, repo-backend-p2-063).

requirements.statement: A copy does not carry over the arrival details (port of entry, arrival date, means of transport, transport identification and transport document reference): the copy's Arrival details show To do.
requirements.why: Arrival is specific to each shipment.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the copy's Arrival details show Complete (trace-e2e-p3-075, trace-e2e-p13-109), though the copy mapper clears the transport block in the record (repo-backend-p2-060).

requirements.statement: A copy does not carry over the transit countries.
requirements.why: The route is specific to each shipment.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the copy's Transit countries show Complete (trace-e2e-p3-075, trace-e2e-p13-109).

requirements.statement: A copy does not carry over the transporter: the copy's Transport details show To do.
requirements.why: The transporter is chosen per shipment.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the copy's Transport details show Complete (trace-e2e-p3-075).

requirements.statement: A copy does not carry over the contact address: the copy's Contact address shows To do.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 asks for the contact address again on each notification.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the copy's Contact address shows Complete (trace-e2e-p3-075, trace-animals-fit-p2-077), though the copy mapper clears the consignment block in the record (repo-backend-p2-061).

requirements.statement: A copy does not carry over uploaded documents: the copy's Upload documents shows To do.
requirements.why: Documents are specific to each shipment.
requirements.deltaNote: Upload documents already shows To do on a copy (trace-e2e-p3-076).

requirements.statement: Copying a notification that is being amended copies its submitted version, not the edits in progress.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copies the saved notification; an unfinished amendment is not yet the notification.
requirements.deltaNote: Today copying an AMEND notification copies its current, edited content (repo-backend-p2-066).

requirements.statement: Copy as new for a notification the trader cannot reach (unknown reference, or a status that cannot be copied such as deleted) changes nothing and returns to the set's own notification list with no message.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 guards the route silently; the 9 October afternoon ruling sends its 'overall dashboard' to the set's own list.
requirements.deltaNote: Copy already returns an unknown notification to the set's list with no banner (repo-frontend-p3-073); the backend refuses unknown (404) and uncopyable (400) sources (repo-backend-p2-037, repo-backend-p2-038).

requirements.statement: Copy as new is checked against the version the trader was looking at: if the notification changed since, nothing is copied and the trader returns to where they started (the dashboard or the notification's view page) with the 'The notification has been updated' banner. A stale copy from the view page must land on the view page, not on a missing check-answers page.
requirements.why: A trader must never copy content different from what they saw; the prototype cannot express concurrent edits.
requirements.deltaNote: The token check and banner exist (repo-frontend-p3-074, repo-backend-p2-040), but a stale copy started from the view page redirects to /notifications/{id}/check-answers?staleAction=1, which no route serves (repo-frontend-p3-075-m1).

requirements.statement: A notification being amended can be deleted (from the amend review's Delete button) in every set that amends, and the backend's soft-delete API description says DRAFT, SUBMITTED and AMEND notifications can be deleted.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 offers Delete during an amendment, and the API must describe what it does.
requirements.deltaNote: The backend and both frontends already delete AMEND notifications (repo-backend-p3-034, repo-frontend-p3-091, repo-plantsfrontend-p3-092), but the API description says only DRAFT and SUBMITTED (repo-backend-p3-035) and no fit spec proves deleting an amending notification (repo-frontend-p3-135-m1, repo-plantsfrontend-p3-133).

requirements.statement: The delete confirmation page identifies the notification in a GOV.UK summary list with the rows 'Reference number', 'Commodity', 'Number' and 'Origin' (the country of origin), in every set (live animals, germinal products and plants).
requirements.why: The trader confirms they are deleting the right notification; the 9 October afternoon ruling gives plants the same layout in the same increment.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the delete page has only a heading, one sentence and two buttons (repo-frontend-p3-092, repo-frontend-p3-093), in plants too (repo-plantsfrontend-p3-085, repo-plantsfrontend-p3-086).

requirements.statement: In the animals sets, the delete page's Commodity row lists each commodity's common name with its species' Latin names in brackets, comma-separated (for example 'Sheep (Ovis Aries), Goat (Capra Hircus)'); for other live mammals each species' common name is used.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's format for naming what was notified.

requirements.statement: In the live-animals set, the delete page's Number row shows the notification's total number of animals.
requirements.why: Animals are counted by head. The 9 October ruling splits this requirement by set; the germinal set's packages count is its own requirement.

requirements.statement: A delete page summary row with no value from the notification falls back to what the set's notification list shows for it, and shows 'Not applicable' when that is empty too, in every set.
requirements.why: Every row shows something, even for an early draft.

requirements.statement: Below the summary the delete page says 'Confirm that you want to delete this notification.', in every set.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's confirmation wording.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the page has no such sentence (repo-frontend-p3-093).

requirements.statement: The delete page warns 'This action cannot be undone.', in every set.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's warning wording.
requirements.deltaNote: Today it reads 'This cannot be undone.' (repo-frontend-p3-093, trace-e2e-p3-060), in plants too (repo-plantsfrontend-p3-086).

requirements.statement: The delete page's red warning button reads 'Yes, delete', in every set.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's button wording.
requirements.deltaNote: Today it reads 'Yes, delete notification' (repo-frontend-p3-095, trace-animals-fit-p3-008), in plants too (repo-plantsfrontend-p3-087).

requirements.statement: Beside 'Yes, delete' the delete page has a plain link 'No, cancel' in the button group, replacing the secondary button 'No, return to dashboard', in every set.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's wording and pattern for not deleting.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the way back is a secondary button-styled link 'No, return to dashboard' (repo-frontend-p3-096, trace-animals-fit-p3-009), in plants too (repo-plantsfrontend-p3-088).

requirements.statement: The delete page's Back link and 'No, cancel' both return to the notification's view page, in every set (plants' check answers view).
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 sends the trader back to the notification they were deleting.
requirements.deltaNote: Today both go to the set's list (repo-frontend-p3-097, trace-animals-fit-p3-010, trace-e2e-p3-063), in plants too (repo-plantsfrontend-p3-088, repo-plantsfrontend-p3-089).

requirements.statement: The delete confirmation page shows no journey strip (status tag and reference) above its heading, in every set; the summary list identifies the notification instead.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 builds the page from GOV.UK components only.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the page shows the journey strip with the status tag and reference (repo-frontend-p3-094-m1, trace-e2e-p3-064).

requirements.statement: The delete confirmation page is titled 'Delete this notification? - Import notification service - GOV.UK' with the level-1 heading 'Delete this notification?', serves every deletable status, and can be opened directly by its address, in every set.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree on the heading.
requirements.deltaNote: Today's delete page already has this title and heading for drafts and submitted notifications (trace-animals-fit-p3-006-m1, trace-animals-fit-p3-013), reached from each card's Delete (trace-animals-fit-p3-001), and plants' delete page has the same heading (repo-plantsfrontend-p3-085).

requirements.statement: Confirming the delete (a POST with the CSRF crumb) soft-deletes the notification: its status becomes DELETED and the record is kept; a repeat is a harmless no-op; a NotificationDeleted (draft) or NotificationSubmissionDeleted (submitted or amending) event is recorded with the actor and organisation id; an unknown reference gets 404. Plants soft-deletes through its own backend the same way.
requirements.why: The real store keeps deleted records for other services and audit; the prototype's outright removal cannot express persistence.
requirements.deltaNote: Delete already soft-deletes through the backend, idempotently, with the events (repo-backend-p3-033, repo-backend-p3-036, repo-backend-p3-040, trace-e2e-p14-078).

requirements.statement: After 'Yes, delete' the trader lands on the set's own notification list (the live-animals set root, the germinal products set root, plants' own list), and the redirect keeps ?deleted=1 in its address.
requirements.why: The 9 October afternoon ruling sends every Design Release 2.1 'overall dashboard' destination, the delete landing included, to the set's own list, replacing the INS landing; the 9 October ruling keeps ?deleted=1 on the redirect (c-198, c-269).
requirements.deltaNote: The live-animals delete already lands on /live-animals?deleted=1 (repo-frontend-p3-099, trace-e2e-p3-066), and plants' on its own list with deleted=1 (repo-plantsfrontend-p3-094); the germinal set gets it with its copy of the feature.

requirements.statement: The deletion success message reads 'Notification has been deleted' in every set (live animals, germinal products and plants): Design Release 2.1's wording for a page that does not know the deleted notification's reference, which the ?deleted=1 redirect does not carry.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's wording; its '<reference> has been deleted' form needs the reference on the list, and the 9 October ruling keeps the redirect's address as ?deleted=1.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the banner is titled 'Notification deleted' and reads 'The notification has been deleted.' (trace-animals-fit-p3-017, trace-animals-fit-p3-018, trace-e2e-p3-068). The banner's 'Success' title is req-1086's.

requirements.statement: A deleted notification no longer appears in the notification list, and searching for its reference finds nothing.
requirements.why: Deleted notifications are gone from the trader's view.
requirements.deltaNote: The deleted notification already disappears from the dashboard and its search (trace-animals-fit-p3-020, trace-e2e-p3-072).

requirements.statement: Opening or posting delete for a notification the trader cannot reach (unknown reference, another session's notification in plants, or a status that cannot be deleted) changes nothing and returns to the set's own notification list with no message, in every set.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 guards the route; the real service must also check the record exists, which the prototype's POST does not; the 9 October afternoon ruling sends the guard to the set's own list.
requirements.deltaNote: Delete already refuses an unknown or non-deletable notification and returns to the set's list with no banner (repo-frontend-p3-100, repo-frontend-p3-101), as plants' does (repo-plantsfrontend-p3-092, repo-plantsfrontend-p3-095).

requirements.statement: The view page shows the notification's answers in the same six numbered sections and cards as the review page (1. About the consignment to 6. Contact address); the card contents follow the review page's requirements.
requirements.why: One rendering of a notification's answers serves review and view.
requirements.deltaNote: Today's notification view already renders the review page's six numbered sections (trace-animals-fit-p3-051); differences inside the cards are carried by the review page's requirements.

requirements.statement: The backend notification API supports the lifecycle: create gives DRAFT with a minted reference; save keeps DRAFT or AMEND; submit takes DRAFT or AMEND to SUBMITTED and stamps submittedAt; amend takes SUBMITTED to AMEND; cancel-amend takes AMEND back to SUBMITTED; copy reads DRAFT, SUBMITTED or AMEND and makes a new DRAFT; soft-delete makes DELETED. Each write advances the concurrency token, takes an optional actor, and callers from outside carry the API key.
requirements.why: Every action in this area rests on these transitions.
requirements.deltaNote: The backend already implements this lifecycle (repo-backend-p2-111), proven through the API (trace-e2e-p14-067, trace-e2e-p14-070, trace-e2e-p14-077).

requirements.statement: A notification is saved as a draft as the trader goes: one record per reference, keeping its created date, without errors or transient page state.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 autosaves drafts; the real service persists each save.
requirements.deltaNote: Each journey page's save already persists the whole record under its reference (repo-tests-p4-095, repo-tests-p4-096, trace-e2e-p14-083).

requirements.statement: The delete and cancel-amendment confirmations, the restored submitted view and a copied notification's overview have no serious or critical WCAG 2 A or AA axe violations, in the animals frontend and in plants.
requirements.why: The service must meet accessibility standards.
requirements.deltaNote: The fit specs already assert this (repo-frontend-p3-123, repo-frontend-p3-127, repo-frontend-p3-132).

requirements.statement: The tests repo's animals specs and page objects for amend, cancel amendment, copy as new and delete assert the Design Release 2.1 behaviour (new copy, dialogs, landing pages and banners) while still asserting ?cancelled=1 and ?deleted=1 on the cancel and delete redirects, keep the smoke-tagged cancel and delete cases, and cover what today goes unproven: deleting an amending notification and the guard redirects.
requirements.why: End-to-end proof must follow the changed behaviour.
requirements.deltaNote: Today's specs assert the current copy ('Yes, delete notification', 'Cancel this amendment?', 'Amending', ?deleted=1, ?cancelled=1) and do not prove a way back from delete (repo-tests-p3-095, repo-tests-p3-075, repo-tests-p3-099).

requirements.statement: Every new or changed string on the delete and cancel-amendment confirmations, the amend confirmation page and the view page has a Welsh entry, in the animals frontend and in plants.
requirements.why: Today's action pages carry Welsh copy, and the frontend's standing rule (req-1659) is that every new or changed piece of user-facing text has a Welsh version of the same shape; Design Release 2.1 is silent on Welsh, so nothing it shows overrides that rule.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the delete and cancel-amend pages have machine-drafted Welsh copy for their current strings (repo-frontend-p3-089, repo-frontend-p3-104), and plants' copies of them too (repo-plantsfrontend-p3-098, repo-plantsfrontend-p3-114).

requirements.statement: Delete and cancel amendment are checked against the version the trader opened, and the dashboard Amend carries a concurrency token.
requirements.why: Recorded for the report: delete and cancel-amend post a token nobody reads, and Amend posts none. Design Release 2.1 does not ask for a fix, so the programme does not make one.

requirements.statement: Soft delete checks that the caller owns the notification or is an admin.
requirements.why: Recorded for the report as an access-control weakness in the backend; Design Release 2.1 does not cover it, so it needs its own ticket.

requirements.statement: Create, save, copy, submit, amend and cancel-amend write audit records attributed to a user.
requirements.why: Recorded for the report: only deletes and replays are audited, and the write endpoints take no user id. Design Release 2.1 does not ask for audit.

requirements.statement: Backend edge cases answer with a client error rather than a server error: copy with a missing token or no content, amend with no fulfilments, a second submit or amend inside the outbox lock window, and submit of an empty notification.
requirements.why: Recorded for the report as backend defects no user journey reaches; Design Release 2.1 does not cover them.

requirements.statement: The place of destination picker's search does not fail with HTTP 500, and the 500 page offers a way back.
requirements.why: Recorded for the report: seen on the copy test's first attempt, it belongs to the address pickers and the error page, not to copying.

requirements.statement: The prototype's own mechanics are reproduced: its session keys and journey resets, page modifier classes, ?reference addressing, seeded review snapshots and their fixed sample data.
requirements.why: Prototype internals with nothing a user sees; the real service persists notifications in the backend and has its own test data.

requirements.statement: Amend for a notification the trader cannot amend (unknown reference, or not Submitted) changes nothing and returns to the set's own notification list with no message, in every set that amends.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 guards the amend route silently; the 9 October afternoon ruling sends its 'overall dashboard' to the set's own list, plants' included.
requirements.deltaNote: The backend refuses an unknown (404) or non-SUBMITTED (400) amend (repo-backend-p2-092, repo-backend-p2-093); no frontend evidence shows what the trader sees.

requirements.statement: The k6 amendment journey in trade-imports-performance-tests expects Amend to land on the notification's amend review instead of its overview hub; it still edits the origin page, then either cancels at cancel-amend (landing on the view page with cancelled=1) or resubmits through the review and the declaration.
requirements.why: Amend moving to the amend review breaks the k6 'amendment started' check, which today expects the hub; ruling 2026-10-09 claim 199 brings the suite into the amend increment (c-225), and cancel-amend keeps its route and ?cancelled=1.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the k6 amend step posts the crumb to <base>/amend and checks it lands on the hub at <base> (repo-perftests-p1-071).

requirements.statement: In the germinal-products set, the delete page's Number row shows the notification's total number of packages.
requirements.why: Germinal products are counted in packages, not by head; the 9 October ruling splits req-1444 into a live half and a germinal half, and keeps the germinal content for the germinal set's copies.

requirements.statement: A copy of a germinal products notification keeps the certified-for answer 'Germinal products'; it is never mapped to 'Further keeping' as an outdated live-animals value would be.
requirements.why: The germinal set sets certified-for to 'Germinal products' when the draft is created, so the copy rule for retired live-animals values must not overwrite it.

requirements.statement: A copy keeps its source's category: copying a germinal products notification makes a germinal products draft (still a GBN-AG reference) that only the germinal set opens, and copying a live-animals notification makes a live-animals draft.
requirements.why: The backend stores the category on the record and each set opens only its own category, so a copy that lost its category would open in the wrong set or not at all.

requirements.statement: After a delete, the set's own notification list it lands on at ?deleted=1 shows the deletion success message at once, in every set (live animals, germinal products and plants); opening the list again without ?deleted=1 shows no deletion message.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 shows the message on the live-animals list; the 9 October afternoon ruling lands the delete there, and the 9 October ruling drops the session flash, so the message travels only with ?deleted=1 (c-269).
requirements.deltaNote: The live-animals list already shows the banner at ?deleted=1 and none on a plain reload (repo-frontend-p3-131, trace-e2e-p3-070-m1), and plants' list shows it at deleted=1 (repo-plantsfrontend-p3-094); the germinal list is the germinal set's copy.

requirements.statement: The deletion success banner does not dismiss itself after 5 seconds: it stays until the trader leaves or reloads the page, in every set.
requirements.why: A message that disappears on a timer can vanish before a screen-reader or slow reader has it (WCAG 2.2.1); the 9 October afternoon ruling keeps success banners on screen, so Design Release 2.1's 5-second dismissal is not built (c-271).
requirements.deltaNote: Today's deletion banner is a standard GOV.UK success notification banner that stays on the page (trace-animals-fit-p3-019).

requirements.statement: No DR1 parity work is built for the delete and amend journeys (DR1 backlog inc-026).
requirements.why: DR1 had neither journey at its root and its dashboard card offered only Copy as new and View; the row's own verifier found that no frontend work follows under either reading of its scope question. Design Release 2.1 is the comparison these journeys are built to.

requirements.statement: In plants, the delete confirmation page's summary list rows ('Reference number', 'Commodity', 'Number', 'Origin') are filled from plants' own notification: its reference, its commodity as plants names it, its quantity, and its country of origin.
requirements.why: The 9 October afternoon ruling mirrors the delete page into plants in the same increment, keeping plants' own data.
requirements.deltaNote: Plants' delete page today has only its heading, one sentence and two buttons (repo-plantsfrontend-p3-085, repo-plantsfrontend-p3-086).

requirements.statement: The plants frontend's own fit specs for delete and cancel amendment assert the changed pages: the delete page's summary, wording, 'Yes, delete', 'No, cancel' and Back link to the view page; the cancel-amendment page's new heading, no paragraph and 'Go back'; and they still assert ?deleted=1, ?cancelled=1, the restored Submitted notification and no serious or critical axe violations.
requirements.why: Plants' fit specs prove its pages today and must follow them in the same increment.
requirements.deltaNote: Today plants' specs assert 'No, return to dashboard' and a Back link to the dashboard on delete, and 'Cancel this amendment?' with its body paragraph on cancel (repo-plantsfrontend-p3-129, repo-plantsfrontend-p3-135).

requirements.statement: The plants frontend offers Copy as new.
requirements.why: Plants has parked Copy as new (its d-062 and d-065 decisions), and the 9 October afternoon ruling leaves it out of plants' view headers; copy as new is built for the animals sets only.

requirements.statement: Plants settles its parked post-submission policy: whether an amended arrival date re-runs the late timing test, whether a first-submission timestamp is kept, and whether a notification the regulator has acted on may be amended or withdrawn.
requirements.why: Recorded for the report: plants parked these as policy questions, and Design Release 2.1 does not answer them; the late flag stays frozen at first submission meanwhile.

conflicts.about: Whether amend, cancel amendment and copy as new are started by links (GET) as the prototype draws them, or by form posts.

positions.says: The amend and cancel-amendment dialogs' confirm buttons and Copy as new are links to GET routes that change state.
State-changing actions are form posts carrying the CSRF crumb (and the concurrency token).
A real constraint the prototype cannot express (validation, authentication) overrides it.
c-189 and inc-120 are kept: the action is a POST with the crumb.
c-189 stands.
Every state change is a form post.

conflicts.outcome: The rulings rank first: a state change is a POST with the CSRF crumb, an authentication constraint the prototype cannot express, and the 9 October afternoon ruling keeps c-189. Each control looks and reads as Design Release 2.1 draws it, but the ones that change state submit a form: 'Yes, continue' on the amend confirmation page, 'Yes, cancel amendment', 'Yes, delete' and Copy as new. Controls that only lead to a confirmation page ('Amend this notification', the card's Amend, 'Cancel amend') are links. The prototype's claim is kept for where each control leads.

conflicts.about: Amend and cancel-amendment confirmations: a custom modal dialog (Design Release 2.1) or a separate confirmation page (today's cancel-amend, the 9 October afternoon ruling).

positions.says: Both confirmations are modal dialogs opened over the review or view page.
The dialog is a custom component; GOV.UK Frontend has no modal, and a confirmation page would keep to the toolbox.
Cancel amendment is a separate GET/POST page at /notifications/{id}/cancel-amend.
The prototype wins by default over what the real services do today.
The amend and cancel confirmation stays a separate page at today's route and carries the pop-up's wording as page content.
The amend and cancel pop-ups wait as one waiting-on-design increment for both animals sets and plants, expected to be dropped.
This replaces c-190's outcome 'build the dialogs as drawn'.
MoJ's Modal dialog is not accepted: it is Experimental and documents no fallback without JavaScript.

conflicts.outcome: The 9 October afternoon ruling ranks first and replaces this conflict's earlier outcome ('build the dialogs as drawn'). The amend and cancel-amendment confirmations are separate pages at the notification's own amend and cancel-amend routes, carrying the pop-ups' wording as page content (req-1391, req-1392, req-1410 to req-1414), in live animals, germinal products and plants. The pop-ups themselves (req-1393) wait as one increment in the waiting-on-design theme, blocked on design question 9 and expected to be dropped, because GOV.UK Frontend has no modal, MoJ's is not accepted and no custom JavaScript copies the prototype. Nothing is overruled: the prototype's dialog claims are what that blocked increment would build, and their wording is built on the pages now.

conflicts.about: Where confirming an amendment lands: the review page (Design Release 2.1) or the overview hub (today).

positions.says: After choosing to amend, the trader goes to the notification's review page.
Amend posts and lands on the notification's hub.
Amend redirects to the notification's task list hub.

conflicts.outcome: The prototype outranks the tests repo and today's traces: amending lands on the amend review. The tests and trace claims stay as the evidence of today's behaviour.

conflicts.about: Whether edits during an amendment are saved to the record, or held only in the session as the prototype does.

positions.says: Nothing is saved automatically while amending, and cancelling leaves edits in the session without writing them back.
Save keeps a notification in AMEND and persists it, with the submitted version held as a snapshot.
A persistence constraint the prototype cannot express overrides it.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling ranks first: the real service keeps saving amendment edits to the AMEND record behind the submitted snapshot. What the trader sees is the same as Design Release 2.1. The prototype claim is not overruled because it also backs draft autosave (req for drafts).

conflicts.about: Whether delete removes the notification (prototype) or soft-deletes it (today).

positions.says: Confirming the delete removes the notification.
Soft delete keeps the record and its content and sets the status to DELETED, publishing an event.
Persistence and cross-service constraints the prototype cannot express override it.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling ranks first: delete stays a soft delete with its events. To the trader it looks the same as the prototype's removal.

conflicts.about: Dashboard card actions: Copy as new and View only (Design Release 2.1's list) or the status-driven set (today).

positions.says: inc-030 rejected: keep the card's status-driven links; do not flatten to Copy as new and View.
A live-animals dashboard row offers Copy as new and View.
Cards show Resume, View, Amend, Copy as new, Cancel amendment and Delete by status.

conflicts.outcome: The DR1 judgement on this same difference outranks the prototype: the cards keep their status-driven actions. The prototype claim is not overruled because it also shows a deleted notification gone from the list.

conflicts.about: Whether DR1's inc-026 (treat the delete and cancel-amend pages as unassessed, raise nothing about their copy) stops the Design Release 2.1 copy changes.

positions.says: Delete and amend may be capabilities DR1 did not draw, so the pages need reviewing against DR2 designs, not DR1.
Until the designer settles scope, raise nothing about the pages' copy, buttons or wording.
The delete page is headed 'Delete this notification?' with Design Release 2.1's summary, wording and buttons.
Whether delete and amend were in DR1's scope is unsettled; only the designer can settle it.
No frontend work follows under either reading of the scope question.

conflicts.outcome: DR1 ranks above the prototype, and its judgement confines itself to the DR1 comparison and sends these pages to a DR2 comparison. Design Release 2.1 is that comparison, so its copy is adopted. Nothing is overruled.

conflicts.about: What a copy carries over: Design Release 2.1's list, the backend copy mapper's list, or everything but documents (what today's pages show).

positions.says: Copy carries import details, what is imported, reasons, additional details, parties and CPH, and clears counts, identifiers, arrival, transit, transporter, documents and contact address.
Copy keeps identification, commodity type and addresses, and resets logistics and per-animal counts, also clearing the internal reference, species, unweaned answer and exit date.
Today a copy's overview shows every task Complete except Upload documents.

conflicts.outcome: The prototype outranks both: a copy carries exactly Design Release 2.1's list, in the record and on the pages alike. Each field that differs is its own requirement. The backend and trace claims stay as evidence of today's behaviour.

conflicts.about: Copying a notification mid-amendment: the submitted version (prototype) or the edits in progress (today).

positions.says: Copy by reference uses the notification's saved snapshot, which an unfinished amendment does not change.
Copying an AMEND notification copies its current, edited content.

conflicts.outcome: The prototype outranks the backend: copy the submitted version. The backend already holds it as the amend snapshot, so no constraint stands in the way.

conflicts.about: Where the guards, the delete and the view page's Back link send the trader: Design Release 2.1's overall dashboard, the INS front door, or the set's own notification list.

positions.says: After a delete the trader lands on the overall dashboard, which shows no banner.
'Yes, delete' returns to the overall dashboard at the mount root.
The overall dashboard the guards and delete return to is titled Dashboard with the h1 Import notification service.
The dashboard is temporary in the animals frontend and moves to trade-imports-ins-frontend.
Delete returns to the live-animals list at /live-animals?deleted=1.
inc-126 (the delete landing on the overall dashboard) is kept because of the service split in DR1's notes.
The live animals notification list stays in the animals frontend; the earlier move to the INS frontend is superseded.
Every page Design Release 2.1 sends to 'the overall dashboard' goes to the set's own notification list instead, including the view's Back link.
A delete lands on the set's own notification list.
A refused amend, copy or cancel goes to the set's own notification list.
The INS front door is reached through the service navigation as today, replacing the INS landing in c-198 and inc-126, and req-1417 and req-1487's 'overall dashboard'.

conflicts.outcome: The 9 October afternoon ruling ranks first: every page Design Release 2.1 sends to the overall dashboard goes to the set's own notification list instead (the live-animals set root, the germinal products set root, plants' own list). That covers the delete landing, the refused amend, copy and cancel-amendment guards, the delete guard and the view page's Back link. The INS front door is reached through the service navigation as today. This replaces the INS landing the 9 October ruling kept for inc-126, and the earlier outcome of this conflict. DR1's note that the dashboard moves to the INS front door is not overruled here, because other areas still cite it for the INS home; the templates ruling supersedes its list move for this programme. Design Release 2.1's guard claims still back the silent redirect, so only the claims naming the overall dashboard as the landing are overruled.

conflicts.about: What the trader sees when Continue on the amend review is refused because an answer is invalid: nothing (the amend trace) or the error summary the draft review shows.

positions.says: Continue on the amend review is silently held: the same page comes back with no error summary or message.
A draft's review lists incomplete sections in a GOV.UK error summary, each linking to its card.
An amendment can only be resubmitted once every task row is fulfilled.
The prototype (Design Release 2.1) wins by default over what the real services do today.

conflicts.outcome: Continue on the amend review is held while any answer is invalid or incomplete (such as an arrival date outside 7 days back to 6 months ahead): the trader stays on the amend review, and, as Design Release 2.1 draws and specifies it, no error summary or error message is shown. The draft review's error summary with a Complete <card> link per incomplete section is not carried over to the amend review: the prototype wins by default, DR1 judged nothing about the amend review, and the only real constraint (an amendment is resubmitted only once complete and valid) is met by the hold itself.

conflicts.about: Whether the amendment's return buttons post the prototype's action=review|continue|hub field or the real service's own fields.

positions.says: req-1403 keeps its content with no action=review|continue|hub field; exit=hub and ?change=1 stay.
The journey's action buttons submit a field named action whose values are continue, hub and review.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling ranks first and the prototype never decides form field names: the three buttons and where each goes are built as Design Release 2.1 draws them, posting the real service's own fields (exit=hub, ?change=1). The prototype's action field is set aside.

conflicts.about: After cancelling an amendment: whether the view page's address keeps ?cancelled=1, and whether today's success banner stays.

positions.says: For inc-121 and req-1416, ?cancelled=1 stays, and req-1479 keeps asserting it.
Cancelling an amendment returns to the view page with no banner or message, and no marker in the address.
Today 'Yes, cancel amendment' redirects to the view with ?cancelled=1 and an alert 'The amendment has been cancelled and the submitted version restored.'

conflicts.outcome: The ruling ranks first on the address: ?cancelled=1 stays on the redirect, because the prototype never decides URL shapes. On what the trader sees, the prototype outranks today's tests: the view page shows no success banner. Nothing is overruled: the prototype claim still backs the absent banner, and the tests claim still backs the kept ?cancelled=1.

conflicts.about: Where the deletion success message shows, now that the session flash is dropped and ?deleted=1 stays on the delete redirect.

positions.says: The deletion message appears on the live-animals list the next time the trader opens it.
After 'Yes, delete' the trader lands on the overall dashboard, which shows no banner.
Moving the success banner to a session flash (req-1087) is dropped; ?deleted=1 stays on the redirect.
inc-126 (the delete landing on the overall dashboard) is kept because of DR1's service split.
Today delete sends the trader to the live-animals list with ?deleted=1, which shows the banner.
A delete lands on the set's own notification list.
inc-126 and inc-140, in the animals-dashboard theme, cover where a delete lands and the banner.

conflicts.outcome: The 9 October afternoon ruling ranks first: the delete lands on the set's own notification list with ?deleted=1, and that list shows the deletion message straight away, which is the list Design Release 2.1 shows it on. With the session flash dropped, the message travels only with ?deleted=1, so opening the list again without it shows none. In plants the same happens on plants' own list. This replaces the earlier outcome that put the message on the INS front door's dashboard.

conflicts.about: Whether the deletion success banner dismisses itself after 5 seconds.

positions.says: The deletion banner is set to dismiss itself after 5 seconds.
Today's deletion banner is a standard GOV.UK success notification banner with role alert that stays on the page.
A real constraint the prototype cannot express overrides it.
inc-126's deletion success banner stays until the trader leaves or reloads the page, because WCAG 2.2.1 rules out a message that leaves on a timer.

conflicts.outcome: The 9 October afternoon ruling ranks first: the deletion success banner does not dismiss itself; it stays until the trader leaves or reloads the page, as today's GOV.UK success notification banner with role alert does, in every set. A message that leaves on a timer can vanish before a screen-reader or slow reader has it (WCAG 2.2.1). Everything else about the banner follows Design Release 2.1.

conflicts.about: Whether a submitted notification's card Amend starts the amendment straight away (today) or goes through the amend confirmation page.

positions.says: Plants' amend landing moves to its review page behind a confirmation page with no pop-up; plants' only Amend today is on its card.
The amend confirmation stays a separate page at today's route.
Keep the card's status-driven links; do not flatten them to Copy as new and View.
The card's Amend posts and starts the amendment straight away.
A plants notification is amended from the dashboard's 'Amend notification REF' button.

conflicts.outcome: The 9 October afternoon ruling ranks first: every way into an amendment goes through the amend confirmation page. The card's Amend, which DR1's judgement keeps on the card with its wording and accessible name, becomes a link to that page instead of posting straight away, in live animals, germinal products and plants. Nothing is overruled: the DR1 judgement still keeps the action on the card, and today's claims are the evidence of what changes. req-1084's 'Amend ... posts' needs the cross-area pass to align with this.
